questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly a destination with different culture and a different academic structure to try something new and different from what i was used to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Generally quite easy to know where go or where to write them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Received most of the assistance when i had to get enrolled to all the courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It did take them a long time getting me enrolled which entailed that I missed some of the first lectures in some courses. Furthermore, I wasn't able to get one of the courses i wanted as it had changed to only be offered another semester, which I was not able to see anywhere beforehand.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Knew someone who had stayed at a big flat where I got a room as well so it was quite easy in my case.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are not really as many social events with people from your class so it can be hard to find new friends when abroad. Thus, it can be beneficial to find a place with some other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a little bit dissatisfied in my particular case of housing but that was only in my specific case which might not be that bad for others.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At first it was quite difficult as the course list I was able to find through UCPH was only for bachelor students which I only find out after the host university rejected my pre-approval.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The general guide to the registration was plenty elaborate and when calling the they were very helpful. They only problem was that it was quite difficult to connect the information from UCPH with the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My registration for classes where quite difficult as I needed very specific courses at two different master, however, I ended up with most of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My best advice would be to start early and write both the host university and the receiving university as you will ensure that you do everything correctly and can save a lot of time from possible misunderstandings.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It did have courses on two different masters but the level varies greatly between all courses and the workload was also disproportionate for some of the courses compared to ECTS points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different as most classes were only around 10 people and we did not really have any lectures but rather just classes. Also there was much greater focus on assignments and attendance which accounted for most of your grades compared to UCPH where the all of the grade  is decided at the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Multinational Accounting, Multinational Financial Management, Economic Growth II, Governments and Markets, Cooperative decision making and social choice, Political Economy, Cooperation and strategy in finance and insurance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cooperative decision making and social choice, Political Economy, and Economic Growth II.
Those were the courses where I actually felt that I learned something valuable and where the work load was more appropriate although it seems a little difficult in the beginning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Did have to buy covers and a pillow and so on the first month as it wasn't a part of the room I'f rented.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally eating out is way cheaper and most of the time i bought food instead of making it myself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mainly saw athletic activities promoted by the host university but through Erasmus there was a lot of cultural and social activities as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely playing a lot of padel and otherwise attend as many of the Erasmus trips and events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Erasmus does some trips in the weekend that I'd really recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took a little while to get adjusted but after a few days walking around in the city you'll be more confident.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: More homeless people and low-level crime such as pick-pockets which is not that normal in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: More relaxed and later dinner times made it feel like i got more out of the day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate more in classes as it counts for a lot of your grade. Focus more on your assignments and don't worry too much about the exams as they are not as difficult as they are at UCPH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience a new culture and a new academic structure.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was unfortunately very sick at most of my stay and the health care system in Spain is not as effecient.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
